packageRules.description: Backend runtime and dev tooling, grouped so one PR runs backend CI once instead of a dozen times.
yt-dlp breaks when YouTube changes, not on a schedule, and a stale one is a broken import rather than a missed feature. Its own PR, immediately.
The web client. Grouped per ecosystem so a bump runs the workflows it can actually affect.

Expo pins its own versions to the SDK, and a native dependency bumped out from under a dev build produces a runtime error, not a red test. These are reviewed by hand, at an SDK upgrade. Every manager, not just npm: a first dry run (2026-09-03) showed Renovate reaching into mobile/modules/mio-media-session/android/build.gradle for androidx.media3, which is exactly the native dependency this rule exists to protect.
A major is a change, not an update: it gets read.

Python is pinned deliberately, and its bump is not a major so the rule above does not catch it. backend/.python-version, backend/Dockerfile and requires-python are kept in step on purpose: the lock spans >=3.12, so a different interpreter can legitimately resolve different packages out of the same uv.lock, and that arrives as changed behaviour rather than a red test. Renovate listed python 3.12 -> 3.14 as a scheduled minor on its first run (2026-09-03), which would have opened unattended. It gets read.
